items.htmltext: Our article “The Importance of Age Inequality for Intersectional Scholarship: The Case of the Workplace” (with Toni Calasanti and Neal King) is published open access in Sociology Compass.
Presenting “From Perk to Norm: The Diffusion of Remote Work and the Divergence of Its Satisfaction and Pay” at the Population Association of America 2027 Annual Meeting in Seattle (April 2027).

Presenting “Not All Moves Are Equal: How Employment and Capital Composition Shape Residential Mobility Strategies” at the Association for Humanist Sociology 50th Annual Meeting at Rutgers University, New Brunswick, NJ (October 2026).
Presenting “Neoliberal Doxa across the World-System: Economic Beliefs in the Global North and South” at the Mid-South Sociological Association 52nd Annual Conference in Huntsville, AL (October 2026).
Began serving as a manuscript reviewer for Social Indicators Research.
Our reskilling-urgency research was featured in VT News: “How urgently do AI-exposed jobs need retraining?” and republished by Technology.org.

Joined the GRASS project as Graduate Research Assistant and Project Manager, working with Dr. Liesel Ritchie on the social dimensions of regenerative grazing (a Virginia Tech–West Virginia University collaboration).
Received a Travel Fund Program award from the Graduate and Professional Student Senate, Virginia Tech, supporting ASA 2026.
Became a graduate affiliate of the Center for Future Work Places and Practices (CFWPP) at Virginia Tech.
Took part in the Summer Institute in Computational Social Science (SICSS) at Stanford University.
Presented “Social Capital and the Timing of Corporate Elite Mobility” at the American Sociological Association 121st Annual Meeting in New York City.
Presented “Pricing Care Labor: The Devaluation of Bodywork and the Intersectional Division of Reproductive Labor” at the Society for the Study of Social Problems 76th Annual Meeting in New York City.

Completed the 2026 ICPSR Summer Program in Quantitative Methods at the University of Michigan, with coursework in causal inference, network analysis, and structural equation modeling, and served as Teaching Assistant for Categorical Data Analysis.
Named a Dean's Graduate Scholar in the College of Liberal Arts and Human Sciences at Virginia Tech, which carries the CLAHS Fellowship Award.
Received a Graduate Student Fellowship from the Center for Humanities at Virginia Tech.
Our paper Mapping Workforce Reskilling Urgency in the Age of AI: Occupational and Geographic Patterns across the United States was published in Telematics and Informatics.
Presented “Social Capital and the Geography of Opportunity” at the Southern Sociological Society 2026 Annual Meeting in Jacksonville, FL.
Presented “Divergent Value Trajectories: Cultural and Economic Liberalization in the United States, 2004–2024” at the 42nd Annual GPSS Research Symposium, Virginia Tech.
Presented “The Moral Economies of Influencer Culture” at the Eastern Sociological Society 96th Annual Meeting in Washington, DC.
Received the Patricia and John Edwards Fellowship Award, Virginia Tech.
Presented “Redistribution Gap: Class, Race and Political Ideology in Shaping Attitudes Toward Inequality” at the Association for Humanist Sociology 49th Annual Meeting in Columbus, OH.
Presented “Economic Precarity, Quality of Work Life, and Social Trust” at the Society for the Study of Social Problems 2025 Annual Meeting in Chicago, IL.

Presented “Public, Private, or Personal: Comparative Impacts of Government, Private, and Self-Employment on Job and Financial Satisfaction” at the Canadian Association for Work and Labour Studies in Hamilton, Ontario.
Presented “Digital Transformation and Work Paradigm's Shift” at the Southern Sociological Society 2025 Annual Meeting in Charlotte, NC.
